1.title: Hello from a new student
1.brief: You are new in an English class. Write a short message to the class group chat. Say hello, give your name and nickname, say where you are from and what your job is.
1.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje al chat del curso para presentarte: nombre, apodo, país y trabajo.
criteria: Use “I am / I’m” at least four times.
Include “my name is” and “my nickname is”.
Use “to be from” for your city or country.
1.model: Hi everyone! My name is Daniela and my nickname is Dani. I'm from Medellín, Colombia. I'm 24 years old and I'm a student. I'm also a nurse at a small hospital. I'm single and I live with my parents. Nice to meet you all! See you on Monday.

1.title: My best friend's profile
1.brief: Write a short profile of your best friend for a class poster. Say his or her name, age, country or city, job and if he or she is married or single.
1.briefEs: Escribe el perfil de tu mejor amigo o amiga para un cartel: nombre, edad, ciudad, trabajo y estado civil.
criteria: Use “he is / she is” correctly in every sentence about your friend.
Use at least three possessive adjectives (my, his, her, their).
Include two words from the unit: friend, neighbour, married / single, job.
1.model: This is my best friend. Her name is Laura and she is 26 years old. She is from Cali, but now she is my neighbour in Bogotá. Her job is interesting: she is a pilot! She is married. Her husband's name is Andrés and he is a teacher. Their dog is Toby. Laura is very nice and funny.

1.title: Questions for a pen pal
1.brief: Write a short email to a new pen pal from another country. Introduce yourself in two sentences, then ask four questions with “to be” (name, country, age, job).
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un nuevo amigo por correspondencia: preséntate y hazle cuatro preguntas con “to be”.
criteria: Four questions with the verb first or a Wh-word: Are you…? What is…? Where are…?
Use a correct greeting and closing (Hi…, Best wishes…).
Use “your” in at least two questions.
1.model:
Hi Emma,

My name is Camilo and I'm from Bucaramanga, Colombia. I'm 19 and I'm a student. What is your full name? Where are you from? How old are you? Are you a student too, or what is your job? Is your family big?

Write soon!
Camilo

1.title: Library card form
1.brief: You want a library card. Complete the form with full sentences: first name, surname, age, city and country, phone number and email.
1.briefEs: Completa el formulario de la biblioteca con oraciones completas: nombre, apellido, edad, ciudad, país, teléfono y correo.
criteria: Use “My name is…” and “I am / I’m” correctly.
Write numbers (age, phone number) correctly.
Include your city and country with “from”.
1.model: My first name is Ana and my surname is Torres. I'm twelve years old. I'm from Quito, in Ecuador. My phone number is 555 0134. My email is ana.torres@example.com. I'm a student in Grade 7 and my school is Colegio Sol. It is near my house.

1.title: Meeting at a party
1.brief: You meet a new classmate at a party. Write a short chat of six or seven lines: names, countries and favourite colour.
1.briefEs: Conoces a un compañero nuevo en una fiesta. Escribe un chat corto de seis o siete líneas: nombres, países y color favorito.
criteria: Use “What’s your name?” and “Where are you from?”.
Answer with “I’m…” and “I’m from…”.
Include “Nice to meet you” once.
1.model:
Hi! I'm Leo. What's your name?
I'm Sara. Nice to meet you!
Nice to meet you, too. Where are you from?
I'm from Chile. And you?
I'm from Peru. Are you a student?
Yes, I am. My favourite colour is green.
Mine is blue. See you in class!

1.title: A welcome note for an exchange student
1.brief: An exchange student, Mia, arrives at your house. Write a short welcome note: your name, your age, your family and one pet.
1.briefEs: Una estudiante de intercambio llega a tu casa. Escribe una nota de bienvenida: tu nombre, edad, familia y una mascota.
criteria: Use “my” and “your” correctly.
Say the jobs of two family members.
Use “is / are” at least five times.
1.model: Hello Mia! Welcome to my house. My name is Pedro and I'm fourteen. I'm your host brother. My mum is a teacher and my dad is a doctor. My sister, Lucía, is nine. Our dog is called Rex. He's very friendly. We are happy to meet you!

1.title: My family's jobs
1.brief: Write about three people in your family: their names, ages and jobs.
1.briefEs: Escribe sobre tres personas de tu familia: nombres, edades y trabajos.
criteria: Use “he is / she is” with a job each time.
Write three ages as words (forty-three).
Use “a” before each job (a nurse).
1.model: I have a small family. My mother's name is Rosa. She is forty and she is a nurse. My father is Carlos. He is forty-three and he is a bus driver. My brother is Andrés. He is sixteen and he is a student. We are a happy family.

1.title: At the immigration desk
1.brief: You arrive in a new country. Write a short dialogue with the immigration officer: your name, country, age and why you are there.
1.briefEs: Llegas a un país nuevo. Escribe un diálogo corto con el oficial de inmigración: tu nombre, país, edad y por qué estás allí.
criteria: Use “What’s your name?” and “Where are you from?”.
Answer with “My name is…”, “I’m from…” and “I’m…”.
Write at least six lines.
1.model:
Officer: Good morning. What's your name?
Traveller: My name is Julián Ortiz.
Officer: Where are you from?
Traveller: I'm from Bogotá, Colombia.
Officer: How old are you?
Traveller: I'm sixteen. I'm a student.
Officer: Why are you here?
Traveller: I'm here for a football tournament. Thank you!

1.title: Hello, new neighbour
1.brief: A new neighbour moves into the flat next to yours. Write him or her a short email to say hello and give some information about you.
1.briefEs: Un vecino nuevo llega al apartamento de al lado. Escríbele un correo corto para saludarlo y decirle algo sobre ti.
criteria: Start with Hi / Dear and finish with Best wishes.
Say your age, city and what you do.
Ask two questions with “to be”.
1.model: Hi Mr López, I'm Julia, your new neighbour. I'm from Cali and I'm twenty-two. I'm a student at the university. My flat is number 5. It's next to your flat. Are you from Bogotá? Is your family here? Come and say hello any time! Best wishes, Julia

1.title: A photo of my class
1.brief: Look at a photo of your class. Describe three classmates and your teacher: names, ages and countries.
1.briefEs: Mira una foto de tu clase. Describe a tres compañeros y al profesor: nombres, edades y países.
criteria: Use “is from” and “are” correctly.
Include three nationalities or countries.
Use “his / her / their” at least twice.
1.model: This is a photo of my class. Tom is from the USA. He is thirteen. Mei is from China and she is twelve. Her best friend is Lucas. He is Brazilian. They are very funny. Their favourite subject is Art. Our teacher is Ms Dell. She is from England and she is very kind. We are a great class.

2.title: My Monday in a message
2.brief: A friend wants to call you on Monday. Write a message describing your Monday routine with times so your friend knows when you are free.
2.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo con tu rutina del lunes y las horas, para que sepa cuándo llamarte.
criteria: Use at least four times with “at” (at 6:00, at noon…).
Use three routine verbs: wake up, get up, have breakfast, finish, take a bus.
Use one frequency word: always, usually.
2.model: Hi Pablo! On Mondays I always wake up at 5:30 and I get up at 5:45. I have breakfast at 6:00 and I take a bus at 6:30. I start work at 7:30. I have lunch at 12:30. I usually finish at 5:00, so call me after 6:00. Bye!

2.title: A routine of someone in my family
2.brief: Describe the daily routine of a family member. Use the third person (he/she) and say what he or she does in the morning, afternoon and evening.
2.briefEs: Describe la rutina diaria de un familiar usando la tercera persona (he/she).
criteria: Every he/she verb has -s or -es (wakes, goes, watches).
Use “in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening”.
Use two words from the unit: early, late, lunch, dinner, weekday.
2.model: My father is a taxi driver. He gets up very early, at 4:30. He has coffee and he leaves home at 5:00. In the morning, he drives around the city. He has lunch at home at 1:00. In the afternoon, he works again. He finishes late, at 8:00. In the evening, he has dinner and watches the news.

2.title: Interview questions about routines
2.brief: Write six questions for a classmate about his or her weekday and weekend routine. Then write your own short answers to two of them.
2.briefEs: Escribe seis preguntas sobre la rutina de un compañero y responde dos de ellas tú mismo.
criteria: Use “do” with I/you/they and “does” with he/she.
Use at least four different Wh-words: what time, when, where, how.
Include “weekday” or “weekend” in two questions.
2.model:
1. What time do you wake up on weekdays?
2. How do you go to work or school?
3. Where do you have lunch?
4. When do you finish your classes?
5. What do you usually do on the weekend?
6. Does your brother get up late on Sundays?

My answers: 1. I wake up at 6:00. 5. I usually visit my grandmother on the weekend.

2.title: My Sunday
2.brief: Write about a normal Sunday in your life, from the morning to the evening. Use times and the present simple.
2.briefEs: Escribe sobre un domingo normal en tu vida, de la mañana a la noche. Usa horas y el presente simple.
criteria: Use at least five times (at nine o’clock…).
Use “I” + verb without -s.
Use “in the morning / afternoon / evening”.
2.model: On Sundays I get up at nine o'clock. I have breakfast with my family at ten. In the morning, I help my mum in the kitchen. We have lunch at one. In the afternoon, I play football with my cousins at three. In the evening, I watch TV and I go to bed at ten.

2.title: My school day, hour by hour
2.brief: Write your school day hour by hour. Use the time at the start of each sentence.
2.briefEs: Escribe tu día de colegio hora por hora. Empieza cada oración con la hora.
criteria: Start each sentence with “At + time”.
Use eight different verbs (get up, have, take, go, do…).
Use “and” or “then” at least twice.
2.model: At 7:00 I get up and then I have breakfast. At 7:30 I take the bus to school. At 8:00 classes start. At 10:30 I have a break and I eat a snack. At 1:00 I have lunch with my friends. At 3:00 I go home. At 4:00 I do my homework and then I play video games. At 9:00 I read a book and I go to bed.

2.title: What do you do after school?
2.brief: Write a message to a friend. Say what you do after school and ask what he or she does.
2.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo. Cuéntale qué haces después del colegio y pregúntale qué hace él o ella.
criteria: Use the present simple with “I” and “he / she”.
Use “and” and “then” to link actions.
End with a question: “What do you do…?”.
2.model: Hi Dani! After school I go home and have lunch. Then I do my homework for an hour. At five I play video games or I draw. My brother doesn't play with me because he works. At seven we have dinner. What do you do after school? Write soon!

2.title: A day in the life of my pet
2.brief: Describe a day in the life of your pet (or an animal you like). Say what it does and at what time.
2.briefEs: Describe un día en la vida de tu mascota (o de un animal que te guste): qué hace y a qué hora.
criteria: Use “he / she / it” + verb with -s or -es.
Include six times.
Use “then” and “in the afternoon”.
2.model: My dog Luna has a busy day. She wakes up at six and she drinks water. At seven she eats her breakfast. Then she goes for a walk with my dad. She sleeps in the afternoon, from two to four. At five she plays with me in the garden. She eats dinner at seven and she goes to bed at nine.

2.title: Weekdays and weekends
2.brief: Write an email to a pen pal. Say how your weekdays are different from your weekends.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo por correspondencia. Cuéntale en qué se diferencian tus días de semana de tus fines de semana.
criteria: Use “I don’t…” at least once.
Use “on Saturdays / on Sundays”.
Ask one question with “do you”.
2.model: Hi Ryan, My weekdays are busy. I get up early, I go to school and I do homework. On Saturdays I don't get up early. I play football in the morning and I visit my grandma. She makes lunch for the family. On Sundays we rest. What do you do at the weekend? Write soon, Sofía

2.title: Opening hours sign
2.brief: Write a sign for a small shop (a bakery, a bookshop, a pharmacy). Say when it opens and closes each day and when it is closed.
2.briefEs: Escribe un cartel para una tienda pequeña (panadería, librería, farmacia). Di cuándo abre y cierra cada día y cuándo está cerrada.
criteria: Include opening and closing times for three different days or groups of days.
Use “opens / closes” correctly.
Say one day when the shop is closed.
2.model: LIBRERÍA LUNA – OPENING HOURS. The shop opens from Monday to Friday at nine o'clock in the morning. It closes at six in the evening. On Saturdays, we open at ten and we close at two. We close for lunch from one to two on weekdays. On Sundays, the shop is closed. Welcome!

2.title: A voice message to Mum
2.brief: You are at school and you can't write. Leave a voice message for your mum (write it down). Say your afternoon schedule: when you finish, where you go and when you get home.
2.briefEs: Estás en el colegio y no puedes escribir. Deja un mensaje de voz a tu mamá (escríbelo). Di tu horario de la tarde: cuándo sales, adónde vas y cuándo llegas a casa.
criteria: Use at least four times (at two o’clock…).
Use the present simple with “I” and “we”.
Start with “Hi Mum” and finish with “Bye”.
2.model: Hi Mum! I finish school at two o'clock today. Then I go to Grandma's house with my cousin. We have lunch there and I do my homework. My football practice starts at four. It finishes at five thirty. I get home at six. Can you pick me up at the park? Bye!

3.title: At the shopping centre
3.brief: You are shopping and your friend is at home. Write a message comparing two things you see (two jackets, two phones…). Ask your friend which one is better.
3.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo comparando dos cosas que ves en una tienda y pregúntale cuál es mejor.
criteria: Use “this one” and “that one”.
Use two comparatives with “than” (cheaper than, more comfortable than).
End with a question: Which one is better?
3.model: Hi Sara! I'm at the mall. I want a new jacket. This one is black and it's cheaper than that one. That one is blue and it's more comfortable, but it's expensive: it costs 200,000 pesos! The blue one is also lighter. Which one is better? Help me!

3.title: Two places to eat
3.brief: Compare two restaurants or cafés in your neighbourhood. Talk about price, size, food and how crowded they are. Say which one you prefer.
3.briefEs: Compara dos restaurantes o cafés de tu barrio (precio, tamaño, comida) y di cuál prefieres.
criteria: At least four comparatives (cheaper, bigger, more crowded, better).
Use “than” correctly in every comparison.
Use one demonstrative: this, that, these or those.
3.model: There are two cafés near my house: Café Luna and El Rincón. Café Luna is bigger than El Rincón, but it is more crowded. El Rincón is cheaper and quieter. The coffee at Café Luna is better, but the cakes at El Rincón are more delicious. I prefer El Rincón because it is more comfortable.

3.title: A product review: my shoes
3.brief: Write a short review of something you bought (shoes, a backpack, a phone). Compare it with your old one. Say if it was a bargain.
3.briefEs: Escribe una reseña corta de algo que compraste y compáralo con el que tenías antes.
criteria: Three comparatives: better / worse, lighter / heavier, cheaper / more expensive.
Use “this / these” for the new thing and “that / those” for the old thing.
Use “to cost” and “a bargain”.
3.model: These are my new running shoes. They cost only 120,000 pesos. They were a bargain! These shoes are lighter than my old shoes and they are more comfortable. Those old shoes were heavier and worse for running. The only problem: the colour is uglier. But I'm happy with them. Five stars!

3.title: At the clothes market
3.brief: Write a short dialogue between a customer and a seller at a clothes market. Ask about prices and use this, that, these and those.
3.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo corto entre un cliente y un vendedor en un mercado de ropa. Pregunta precios y usa this, that, these y those.
criteria: Use “How much is / are…?” correctly.
Use this, that, these and those at least once each.
Use one comparative (cheaper, bigger…).
3.model:
A: Hello! How much is this T-shirt?
B: It's ten dollars.
A: Do you have this T-shirt in blue?
B: Yes, here you are.
A: And those shoes?
B: They're thirty dollars.
A: That's expensive! Do you have cheaper shoes?
B: Yes, these shoes are twenty dollars.
A: They're nice. I want these, please. Can I pay by card?
B: Sorry, only cash.

3.title: Two bikes compared
3.brief: Compare your bike with a friend’s bike, or two bikes in a shop. Use comparatives: faster, lighter, more expensive…
3.briefEs: Compara tu bicicleta con la de un amigo, o dos bicicletas de una tienda. Usa comparativos: faster, lighter, more expensive…
criteria: Use “-er than” with short adjectives.
Use “more … than” with long adjectives.
Give your opinion at the end.
3.model: My bike is old, but Carla's bike is new. Her bike is lighter than mine and it is faster. The seat of her bike is more comfortable. Her bike is more expensive than my bike, too. My bike is cheaper and it is stronger, so it is better for the mountains. I like my bike.

3.title: My birthday wish list
3.brief: Write a wish list for your birthday with six things. Use this, that, these and those and say a colour or a size for each thing.
3.briefEs: Escribe una lista de deseos para tu cumpleaños con seis cosas. Usa this, that, these y those y di un color o un tamaño de cada cosa.
criteria: Use this / that for one thing and these / those for two or more.
Use a colour or size word for each thing.
Use “I want / I like / I love”.
3.model: My birthday wish list: I want this blue backpack. I like that red bike over there. I want these black football boots. I love those big headphones on the shelf. I also want this small book about dogs. Please buy that big chocolate cake!

3.title: Choosing a present
3.brief: You and a friend look at two presents for your teacher. Write a chat. Say which one is bigger, cheaper or nicer, and decide using “this one” and “that one”.
3.briefEs: Tú y un amigo miran dos regalos para su profesora. Escribe un chat. Di cuál es más grande, más barato o más bonito, y decidan usando “this one” y “that one”.
criteria: Use two comparatives.
Use “this one” and “that one”.
Decide at the end.
3.model:
A: Look! This book is cheaper than that scarf.
B: Yes, but the scarf is nicer. It's softer.
A: The book is more useful. Ms Ríos loves reading.
B: True! And this book is bigger than the other one.
A: OK, let's buy this one.
B: Good idea! It's only twelve dollars.

3.title: A message to a shop
3.brief: Write a message to a shop. Ask about some trainers in the window: size, price and when you can come.
3.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a una tienda. Pregunta por unos tenis de la vitrina: talla, precio y cuándo puedes ir.
criteria: Use “those” for the trainers.
Ask “How much are they?” and “Do you have…?”.
Use please and thank you.
3.model: Hello, I want to ask about those white trainers in your window. Do you have them in size 38? How much are they? Are they cheaper this week? Is the sale still on? I can come on Saturday morning. Please reply soon. Thank you, Paula Ríos

3.title: Football or basketball?
3.brief: Compare two sports or two hobbies. Say which one is easier, faster, more popular or more exciting.
3.briefEs: Compara dos deportes o dos pasatiempos. Di cuál es más fácil, más rápido, más popular o más emocionante.
criteria: Use “more … than” at least twice.
Use two short comparatives (faster, bigger).
Give your opinion with “I think…”.
3.model: Football and basketball are both fun, but they are different. Football is more popular than basketball in my country. A football team is bigger than a basketball team. Football games are longer. Basketball is faster and the ball is bigger. I think football is easier, but basketball is more exciting than football.

3.title: Big sale sign
3.brief: Write a sign for a clothes shop sale. Include prices, colours, the shop address and opening hours.
3.briefEs: Escribe un cartel para la rebaja de una tienda de ropa. Incluye precios, colores, la dirección y el horario.
criteria: Use these / those with plural clothes.
Write at least three prices.
Include opening hours (from nine to seven).
3.model: BIG SALE! Everything is cheap this week! These jeans are only $15. Those blue jackets are $25. This red dress is $18. Look at these shoes: two for $30! Come to Moda Fácil, next to the bank. We are open from nine to seven. Don't miss it!

4.title: An invitation to lunch
4.brief: Write a short message to invite a friend to lunch on Saturday. Say where and when, and ask if he or she would like to come.
4.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje para invitar a un amigo a almorzar el sábado: dónde, cuándo y si quiere ir.
criteria: Use “Would you like to…?” at least once.
Use two object pronouns (me, you, him, her, us, them).
Include “free”, “together” or “to meet”.
4.model: Hi Juan! Are you free on Saturday? Would you like to have lunch with me? My sister is in town and I want you to meet her. We can go to the Italian restaurant near the park. We can meet there at 1:00 and eat together. Call me or send me a message. See you!

4.title: Ordering for the group
4.brief: Write a short dialogue in a café between a waiter and two friends. The waiter offers things and the friends order politely.
4.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo corto en un café entre un mesero y dos amigos que piden con cortesía.
criteria: The waiter uses “Would you like…?” twice.
The friends use “I’d like…, please” and “thank you”.
Use at least two object pronouns (it, them, us).
4.model:
Waiter: Good afternoon. Would you like a table for two?
Ana: Yes, please.
Waiter: Would you like something to drink?
Ana: I'd like a lemonade, please.
Tomás: Can I have a coffee? Can you bring it with milk, please?
Waiter: Of course. Would you like the cakes? I can show you them.
Tomás: Yes, please. Thank you!

4.title: Can you give me a hand?
4.brief: You are moving to a new flat. Write a message to a neighbour asking for help. Offer something in return.
4.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a tu vecino pidiéndole ayuda con tu trasteo y ofrécele algo a cambio.
criteria: Ask a yes/no question with “Can you…?” or “Would you…?”.
Use the expression “give me a hand”.
Offer something with “Would you like…?”.
4.model: Hello Mrs. Rojas! I'm moving to apartment 302 on Sunday. Can you give me a hand with the big boxes? Maybe your son can help us too. It takes one hour. Would you like to have dinner with me after that? I can make arepas for you. Thank you!

4.title: Can I help you?
4.brief: Your friend is sick at home. Write a message to offer help: homework, food and a phone call.
4.briefEs: Tu amiga está enferma en casa. Escribe un mensaje para ofrecerle ayuda: tareas, comida y una llamada.
criteria: Use “Can I…?” and “I can…” for offers.
Use “Would you like…?” once.
Finish with a kind wish (Get well soon!).
4.model: Hi Camila! I know you are sick. Can I help you? I can bring your homework to your house. Would you like some soup? My mum can make chicken soup. I can also lend you my Maths book. Can I call you tonight? Get well soon! Your friend, Paula

4.title: A bake sale order form
4.brief: Your school has a bake sale. Fill in the order form with full sentences: what you would like, how many, and your name and class.
4.briefEs: Tu colegio hace una venta de postres. Completa el formulario de pedido con oraciones completas: qué quieres, cuántos y tu nombre y curso.
criteria: Use “I’d like…” or “Can I have…?”.
Write two quantities (two, three…).
Include your name and class.
4.model: Hello! I'd like two chocolate muffins and one lemon cake, please. Can I have a bottle of orange juice, too? I don't want any biscuits. My name is Rosa Peña and I'm in Class 6B. I can pay now, with cash. Thank you very much!

4.title: A favour for my neighbour
4.brief: You are not at home on Saturday. Write a note to your neighbour to ask for a favour: please take a parcel for you.
4.briefEs: No estarás en casa el sábado. Escribe una nota a tu vecina para pedirle un favor: que reciba un paquete por ti.
criteria: Use “Can you…?” and “Can I…?”.
Offer something in return (I can bring you…).
Use please and thank you.
4.model: Dear Mrs Peña, I'm Tom from flat 6. Can you help me, please? I'm not at home on Saturday. Can you keep my parcel for me? It's a small box from my aunt. Can I get it on Sunday morning? I can bring you some cake as a thank-you. Thank you very much! Tom

4.title: A polite email to my teacher
4.brief: You can’t come to class on Friday. Write a short, polite email to your teacher. Say why and ask for the homework.
4.briefEs: No puedes ir a clase el viernes. Escribe un correo corto y cortés a tu profesor. Di por qué y pide la tarea.
criteria: Start with Dear Mr / Ms and finish with Best wishes.
Use “I can’t” and “Can you…?”.
Give one reason.
4.model: Dear Mr Ortiz, I'm sorry, but I can't come to class on Friday. I have a doctor's appointment. Can you give me the homework, please? Can I do the test on Monday? My mum can write you a note. Thank you for your help. Best wishes, Daniel Mora

4.title: Offering food at a party
4.brief: Write a dialogue at a party. One person offers drinks and food, the other accepts or says no politely.
4.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo en una fiesta. Una persona ofrece bebidas y comida y la otra acepta o rechaza con cortesía.
criteria: Use “Would you like…?” twice.
Use “Yes, please” and “No, thank you”.
Use “Can I have…?” once.
4.model:
Mia: Would you like some juice, Tom?
Tom: Yes, please. Can I have a small glass?
Mia: Sure. Would you like a sandwich, too?
Tom: No, thank you. I'm not hungry. But can I have some cake?
Mia: Of course! Chocolate or vanilla?
Tom: Chocolate, please.
Mia: Here you are. Enjoy the party!
Tom: Thank you, Mia. It's a great party!

4.title: A request to the hotel
4.brief: You are in a hotel. Write a message to reception: you need more towels and a pillow, and you want breakfast in your room.
4.briefEs: Estás en un hotel. Escribe un mensaje a recepción: necesitas más toallas y una almohada, y quieres el desayuno en tu habitación.
criteria: Use “Can you…?” for requests.
Use “I need…” and “I’d like…”.
Say your room number and thank the staff.
4.model: Hello, this is room 204. Can you help me, please? I need two more towels and one more pillow. Can you bring them to my room? Also, can I have breakfast in my room tomorrow? I'd like eggs, bread and orange juice. Thank you very much. Mr and Mrs Vega

4.title: Help in a card shop
4.brief: Write a dialogue in a card shop. You want a birthday card for your sister. Ask for help, ask the price and ask for an envelope.
4.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo en una tienda de tarjetas. Quieres una tarjeta de cumpleaños para tu hermana. Pide ayuda, pregunta el precio y pide un sobre.
criteria: Start with “Excuse me, can you help me?”.
Use “Would you like…?” in the seller’s lines.
Use please and thanks.
4.model:
A: Excuse me, can you help me?
B: Of course. What do you need?
A: I want a birthday card for my sister.
B: Would you like a funny card or a nice card?
A: A funny one, please. How much is this card?
B: It's three dollars.
A: Can I have it with an envelope?
B: Sure. Anything else?
A: No, thanks.

5.title: What's happening at home?
5.brief: It is Sunday afternoon. Write a message to a friend describing what everybody in your house is doing right now.
5.briefEs: Describe en un mensaje lo que está haciendo cada persona en tu casa en este momento.
criteria: Five verbs in the present continuous (is cooking, are watching…).
Use “at the moment” or “right now”.
Name three family members (parents, cousin, aunt…).
5.model: Hi Caro! It's crazy here at the moment. My mother is cooking sancocho and my father is helping her. My grandparents are watching a football match. My little cousin is playing with the dog and my aunt is talking on the phone. And me? I'm writing to you! What are you doing right now?

5.title: My family in numbers
5.brief: Describe your big family using quantifiers. Say how many people there are and what nearly all, many, not many or no one does.
5.briefEs: Describe a tu familia usando cuantificadores como all, nearly all, many, few, no one.
criteria: Use four different quantifiers (all, nearly all, many, not many, few, no one).
Use “no one” with a singular verb (no one lives…).
Include words like cousins, aunts, uncles, only child.
5.model: My family is very big. I have twelve cousins, six aunts and five uncles. Nearly all my cousins live in Barranquilla. Many of them are students. Not many of my aunts work outside the house. All my uncles love football. Few people in my family speak English. No one is an only child — except me!

5.title: Questions to an old friend
5.brief: Write a short email to a friend you have not seen for a long time. Tell him or her one thing you are doing these days and ask four questions in the present continuous.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un viejo amigo: cuéntale qué estás haciendo y hazle cuatro preguntas en presente continuo.
criteria: Four present continuous questions (Are you working…? What are you doing…?).
One sentence about yourself with “at the moment”.
Correct use of am / is / are in every question.
5.model:
Hi Felipe,

How are you? At the moment I'm living in Pereira and I'm studying English. What are you doing these days? Are you still working at the bank? Is your sister living with you? Are your parents looking after your little brother?

Write back soon,
Mariana

5.title: Describe a family photo
5.brief: Choose one of the three family photos in Unit 5 (the Ortiz, Herrera or multicultural family). Describe it: who the people are, how they are related, where they are and what they are doing and wearing right now.
5.briefEs: Elige una de las fotos familiares de la unidad y descríbela: quién es quién, qué parentesco tienen y qué están haciendo.
criteria: Use at least five family words (uncle, cousin, grandmother…).
Use the present continuous at least four times (is smiling, are sitting…).
Use 's for relationships (Mariana's brother).
Use one quantifier: all, many, no one…
5.model: This is the Herrera family. They are in the garden of the grandparents' house. Rogelio, the grandfather, is wearing a cap and glasses. His wife, Isabel, is standing next to him. Fernando and Mariana are the parents. Mariana's brother, Daniel, is visiting with his daughter Sofía. The children, Simón and Emilia, are sitting on the grass. Max, the dog, is lying near them. All of them are smiling!

5.title: My own family photo
5.brief: Think of a photo of your own family (or imagine one). Describe it as if you are showing it to a new friend: who is in it, how they are related to you, where you are and what everyone is doing.
5.briefEs: Describe una foto de tu familia como si se la mostraras a un amigo nuevo.
criteria: Start with 'This is a photo of…'.
Use 's at least twice (my mum's sister…).
Use the present continuous for what people are doing in the photo.
Finish with one sentence about how you feel about the photo.
5.model: This is a photo of my family at my cousin's wedding. My mum and dad are standing in the middle. My dad is wearing a grey suit. My mum's sister, Gloria, is on the left and she is laughing. My brother is holding his baby daughter, my niece Sara. I'm standing at the back next to my grandmother. Everyone is dancing or smiling. I love this photo because the whole family is together.

5.title: A Sunday in the park
5.brief: Imagine you are in a park on Sunday. Describe what six different people or animals are doing right now.
5.briefEs: Imagina que estás en un parque un domingo. Describe qué hacen en este momento seis personas o animales.
criteria: Use the present continuous (is / are + -ing) at least six times.
Describe six different actions.
Use one sentence with “are” and a plural subject.
5.model: It's Sunday afternoon in the park. A boy is flying a kite and his dad is helping him. Two girls are riding their bikes. An old man is reading a newspaper on a bench. A dog is running after a ball. Some children are eating ice cream. The sun is shining and everybody is happy.

5.title: A video call with Grandma
5.brief: You are on a video call with your grandmother. Tell her what you and your family are doing right now and ask what she is doing.
5.briefEs: Estás en una videollamada con tu abuela. Cuéntale qué hacen tú y tu familia ahora mismo y pregúntale qué hace ella.
criteria: Use “I’m” + verb-ing at least twice.
Use “is / are” for two other family members.
Ask “What are you doing?”.
5.model: Hi Grandma! I'm in my room now. I'm doing my homework and I'm listening to music. Mum is cooking dinner and Dad is watching TV. My sister isn't studying. She's playing a game! What are you doing? Are you watching your favourite programme?

5.title: A football commentary
5.brief: You are a radio reporter at a school football match. Say what the players and the fans are doing right now.
5.briefEs: Eres un reportero de radio en un partido de fútbol escolar. Di qué hacen los jugadores y los hinchas en este momento.
criteria: Use the present continuous for at least five actions.
Use at least two player names.
Use “now” or “right now” once.
5.model: Welcome to the school match! Right now, Dani is running with the ball. Tomás is shouting to his friend. The goalkeeper is waiting near the goal. Now Pablo is kicking the ball! The fans are singing and the coach is standing near the line. Oh no, the ball is going over the wall!

5.title: Greetings from the beach
5.brief: You are on holiday at the beach. Write a postcard to a friend. Say what the weather is like and what you and your family are doing.
5.briefEs: Estás de vacaciones en la playa. Escribe una postal a un amigo. Di cómo está el clima y qué hacen tú y tu familia.
criteria: Use “It’s sunny / hot…” for the weather.
Use the present continuous for three actions.
Start with Dear / Hi and finish with your name.
5.model:
Hi Nico! Greetings from Santa Marta! It's hot and sunny. I'm sitting on the sand and I'm drinking coconut water. My parents are swimming in the sea. My little brother is building a sand castle. We're having a great time. Big hugs,
Wendy

5.title: Questions about a picture
5.brief: Look at a picture of a busy street (or imagine one). Write eight questions about what the people are doing.
5.briefEs: Mira una imagen de una calle concurrida (o imagina una). Escribe ocho preguntas sobre lo que hacen las personas.
criteria: Use “What is / are … doing?” once.
Use two Yes / No questions (Is the man…?).
Use a question mark every time.
5.model: What is the girl doing? Is the man reading a book? Where are the children playing? Are they wearing hats? Who is talking on the phone? Why is the dog barking? Is the woman carrying a bag? What are the boys eating?

5.title: A traffic report
5.brief: You are a radio reporter in the morning. Describe the traffic and what people are doing in the city right now.
5.briefEs: Eres un reportero de radio en la mañana. Describe el tráfico y lo que hace la gente en la ciudad ahora mismo.
criteria: Use the present continuous at least five times.
Use two weather or traffic words (rain, slowly, busy).
Start with “Good morning”.
5.model: Good morning, listeners! It's seven o'clock and the city is waking up. It's raining, so the traffic is moving slowly. Many buses are leaving the station and some children are waiting at the bus stops. A taxi driver is waiting near the bridge. People are walking to work with their umbrellas. Be careful on the roads today!

6.title: My free time
6.brief: Write a short paragraph about your hobbies. Say how often you do each activity using different adverbs of frequency.
6.briefEs: Escribe un párrafo sobre tus pasatiempos y di con qué frecuencia los practicas.
criteria: Five different frequency words (always, usually, sometimes, hardly ever, never).
Put the adverb before the main verb and after “be”.
Use “once / twice a week” at least once.
6.model: In my free time I'm really into music. I usually play the guitar in the evening and I practise twice a week with a band. I sometimes go swimming on Saturdays. I hardly ever watch TV because it's boring for me. I'm never at home on Sunday afternoons: I always visit my friends.

6.title: A club profile
6.brief: You want to join a sports or hobby club. Write a short profile for the club website: your hobby, how often you practise and how good you are.
6.briefEs: Escribe un perfil corto para unirte a un club: tu pasatiempo, con qué frecuencia lo practicas y qué tan bueno eres.
criteria: Use “good at” or “not very good at”.
Use “how often” information with an adverb or “once a week”.
Use “to spend time + -ing” once.
6.model:
Name: Julián Pérez
Hobby: chess
I'm into chess and I'm quite good at it. I play online almost always after dinner and I practise with my uncle once a week. I spend a lot of time reading about famous games. I'm not very good at fast games, so I want to learn!

6.title: A survey about free time
6.brief: Write a survey of six questions with “how” (how often, how much, how good, how long…) about free time. Then answer two questions with short answers.
6.briefEs: Escribe una encuesta de seis preguntas con “how” sobre el tiempo libre y responde dos de ellas.
criteria: Six questions with “how” + another word.
Use two different short answers (Yes, I do. / Not very well.).
Include “free time” and “hobby”.
6.model:
Free time survey
1. How often do you do exercise?
2. How long do you spend on your phone every day?
3. How good are you at cooking?
4. How many hobbies do you have?
5. How well do you dance?
6. How much free time do you have on weekdays?
My answers: 1. Twice a week. 5. Not very well!

6.title: A letter to the school nurse
6.brief: The school nurse asks about your habits. Write a short letter: how often you eat fruit, drink water, play sport and go to bed early.
6.briefEs: La enfermera del colegio pregunta por tus hábitos. Escribe una carta corta: con qué frecuencia comes fruta, tomas agua, haces deporte y te acuestas temprano.
criteria: Use four different frequency adverbs (always, usually, sometimes, never…).
Put the adverb before the main verb (I often go…).
Use “I’m not good at…” once.
6.model:
Dear Nurse Gómez,

I usually eat fruit at breakfast. I always drink water at school and I sometimes play football after class. I never eat sweets in the morning. I often go to bed late, at eleven, because I watch videos. I'm not good at sleeping early! I want to change that.

Best wishes,
Alma Ruiz

6.title: I'm good at...
6.brief: Write a short profile of what you can do well and what you can’t do well. Use can, can’t, good at and well.
6.briefEs: Escribe un perfil corto de lo que haces bien y lo que no haces bien. Usa can, can’t, good at y well.
criteria: Use “I can…” and “I can’t…”.
Use “I’m good at + -ing” once.
Use an adverb of manner (well, fast, badly).
6.model: I'm good at swimming and I can swim very fast. I can also draw well, but I can't sing. I'm bad at Maths, so I study hard. My best friend is good at cooking. She can make pizza and cakes. I can't cook, but I can wash the dishes quickly!

6.title: A talent show form
6.brief: Fill in an application form for the school talent show: what you can do, how well you do it and how often you practise.
6.briefEs: Completa un formulario para el concurso de talentos del colegio: qué sabes hacer, qué tan bien lo haces y con qué frecuencia practicas.
criteria: Use “I can…” and “I can’t…”.
Use one adverb of manner (well, fast, badly).
Say how often you practise (every day, twice a week).
6.model: My name is Gabriela and I'm twelve. I can sing and I can play the piano. I sing well, but I play the piano badly. I can't dance. I practise the piano every day for twenty minutes. I practise singing twice a week with my teacher. I'd like to sing a Colombian song in the show.

6.title: My best friend's skills
6.brief: Describe what your best friend can do and how well he or she does these things.
6.briefEs: Describe lo que tu mejor amigo puede hacer y qué tan bien lo hace.
criteria: Use “he / she can” and “he / she can’t”.
Use three adverbs of manner (well, quickly, carefully).
Use “is good at” once.
6.model: My best friend Tomás is very talented. He can play the guitar well and he sings beautifully. He is also good at football. He runs quickly and he passes the ball carefully. But he can't swim, so he always stays near the edge of the pool. I think he is great.

6.title: Weekend habits chat
6.brief: Write a chat with a friend about your weekend habits. Ask and answer questions with “How often…?”.
6.briefEs: Escribe un chat con un amigo sobre tus hábitos de fin de semana. Pregunta y responde con “How often…?”.
criteria: Use “How often do you…?” twice.
Answer with always, often, sometimes or never.
Write at least six lines.
6.model:
A: How often do you go to the cinema?
B: I sometimes go. And you?
A: I rarely go. I play video games every day.
B: Wow! I never play on school days. I only play on Saturdays.
A: How often do you go to the park?
B: I often go on Sundays with my dog.

6.title: My training diary
6.brief: Write about a sport or hobby you practise: which days you practise, how often you win or lose, and how well you play.
6.briefEs: Escribe sobre un deporte o pasatiempo que practicas: qué días practicas, con qué frecuencia ganas o pierdes y qué tan bien juegas.
criteria: Use three frequency expressions (every Tuesday, twice a month, sometimes).
Use two adverbs of manner (well, quickly, badly).
Write in the first person with “I”.
6.model: I play basketball in a team. We practise every Tuesday and Thursday after school. I usually play well, but I sometimes miss easy shots. I run quickly, so I often score in the second half. Our team wins twice a month. I never miss a practice because I love the sport. On Saturdays I rest or I play with my brother.

7.title: Yesterday in five lines
7.brief: Write a short diary entry about what you did yesterday, from the morning to the night.
7.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre lo que hiciste ayer, de la mañana a la noche.
criteria: Six verbs in the past simple, at least two irregular (went, had, bought).
Use sequence words: then, after that.
Use one sentence with “was” or “were”.
7.model: Yesterday was a busy day. I got up at 6:00 and I went to work by bus. At noon I had lunch with my friend Paula. Then I bought a present for my mother. After that, I arrived home at 7:00. I cooked pasta and I watched a film. It was interesting. I was very tired at night.

7.title: A postcard from my trip
7.brief: Write a postcard to a friend about a short trip you took last weekend. Say where you went, where you stayed, what you did and how it was.
7.briefEs: Escribe una postal a un amigo sobre un viaje corto del fin de semana pasado.
criteria: Use “last weekend” or “two days ago”.
Use “was / were” to describe the place and people.
Include “to stay”, “to travel” and “to have a great time”.
7.model:
Dear Lucía,

Last weekend I travelled to Villa de Leyva with my cousins. We stayed in a small hotel near the main square. The town was beautiful and the people were very friendly. On Saturday we visited a museum and on Sunday we rode bikes. We had a great time!

Love,
Valeria

7.title: Did you have a good weekend?
7.brief: Write a message to a friend asking about his or her weekend. Use five past simple questions with “did” and one with “was”.
7.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo preguntando por su fin de semana con preguntas en pasado.
criteria: Five questions with “did” + base verb (Did you go…? Where did you stay?).
One question with “was” or “were”.
No “did” with the verb in past (not “Did you went…”).
7.model: Hi Nico! How was your weekend? Did you go to the concert on Saturday? Who did you go with? Was it crowded? What time did you get home? Did you see Mateo there? And what did you do on Sunday? Tell me everything!

7.title: My last birthday
7.brief: Write about your last birthday: where you were, who came, what you ate and what you did.
7.briefEs: Escribe sobre tu último cumpleaños: dónde estabas, quién vino, qué comiste y qué hiciste.
criteria: Use at least five past simple verbs.
Use “was / were” once.
Use “then” and “after that”.
7.model: My last birthday was on a Saturday. I was at home with my family and four friends. My mum made a chocolate cake and my dad cooked hamburgers. We played games in the garden. Then we watched a film. After that, my friends went home. I received a new football from my uncle.

7.title: A thank-you email after a trip
7.brief: Your class visited a museum last week. Write a thank-you email to the guide: where you went, what you saw and what you liked.
7.briefEs: Tu clase visitó un museo la semana pasada. Escribe un correo de agradecimiento al guía: adónde fueron, qué vieron y qué te gustó.
criteria: Use five past simple verbs.
Use “Thank you for…” once.
Start with Dear and finish with Best wishes.
7.model:
Dear Ms Alvarado,

Thank you for the tour last Friday. We visited the old city museum and we saw many beautiful paintings. I liked the big ship model the most. You told us interesting stories and we laughed a lot. After the tour, we had lunch in the park. It was a fantastic day!

Best wishes,
Diana Mora

7.title: A message to a friend who was absent
7.brief: A friend was absent from class yesterday. Write a message to say what you did in class and what homework the teacher gave.
7.briefEs: Un amigo faltó a clase ayer. Escribe un mensaje para contarle qué hicieron en clase y qué tarea dejó el profesor.
criteria: Use five past simple verbs.
Use “First”, “Then” and “After”.
Ask “Did you…?” once.
7.model: Hi Nora! You missed a great class yesterday. First, we read a short story and we answered questions. Then we played a vocabulary game. I won! After the break, Mr Silva gave us homework: two exercises on page 40. We also wrote our names for the school trip list. Did you feel better? Call me later!

7.title: My grandmother's life
7.brief: Write a short biography of an older person in your family: where she or he was born, where she or he lived and what job she or he had.
7.briefEs: Escribe una biografía corta de una persona mayor de tu familia: dónde nació, dónde vivió y qué trabajo tuvo.
criteria: Use “was born”.
Use six past simple verbs.
Use “When she / he was…” once.
7.model: My grandmother Rosa was born in a small village in 1950. She lived there with her parents and five brothers. She walked to school every day. When she was eighteen, she moved to the city and worked in a bakery. She met my grandfather there and they got married. They had three children. Today she lives near us and she loves cooking.

7.title: Questions about last night
7.brief: Your friend went to a concert last night. Write eight questions to ask about it.
7.briefEs: Tu amigo fue a un concierto anoche. Escribe ocho preguntas para preguntarle sobre eso.
criteria: Use “Did you…?” at least three times.
Use “What / Where / Who / When did you…?” at least twice.
Use the base verb after “did”.
7.model: Did you buy a T-shirt at the concert? Who did you go with? Where did you sit? Did you like the music? What time did it finish? How did you get home? Did you take photos? What did you eat?

7.title: A story about a lost wallet
7.brief: Write a very short story in the past: someone lost a wallet and someone else found it. What happened?
7.briefEs: Escribe una historia muy corta en pasado: alguien perdió una billetera y otra persona la encontró. ¿Qué pasó?
criteria: Use at least six past simple verbs.
Use “first”, “then” and “finally”.
Include one line of dialogue.
7.model: Last Monday, Sara found a wallet on the bus. First she looked inside. There was an ID card and a phone number. Then she went to the bus driver and he called the owner. Finally, an old man came to the bus station. 'Thank you!' he said. He gave Sara a big smile and some chocolate.

8.title: My neighbourhood
8.brief: Describe your neighbourhood for a new classmate. Say what there is and where things are.
8.briefEs: Describe tu barrio para un compañero nuevo: qué hay y dónde están las cosas.
criteria: Use “there is” with singular and “there are” with plural nouns.
Use three prepositions of place: next to, between, across from, on the corner.
Describe the place as quiet / noisy or crowded.
8.model: I live in Chapinero, in Bogotá. It's a crowded but nice neighbourhood. There is a big park across from my building. There are three cafés on my block and there is a bakery on the corner. The supermarket is between the bank and the pharmacy. There aren't many trees, but there are a lot of restaurants.

8.title: A room for rent
8.brief: Write an advertisement for a room in your flat. Describe the room, the furniture and what is within walking distance.
8.briefEs: Escribe un anuncio para arrendar una habitación: describe la habitación, los muebles y lo que hay cerca.
criteria: Use “there is / there are” three times.
Use “a few” with countable and “a little” with uncountable nouns.
Include “furniture” and “within walking distance”.
8.model: ROOM FOR RENT in Laureles, Medellín. It's a quiet, sunny room with new furniture: there is a bed, a desk and a big wardrobe. There are a few shelves for books. There is a little space for a bike. The metro station and two supermarkets are within walking distance. Call Marta: 300 123 4567.

8.title: Questions about a new city
8.brief: You are moving to a new city. Write an email to a friend who lives there. Ask about the neighbourhood using “how much”, “how many” and “is there / are there”.
8.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo que vive en otra ciudad preguntando por su barrio con how much / how many / is there.
criteria: Two questions with “How many…?” + plural noun.
One question with “How much…?” + uncountable noun.
Two questions with “Is there…?” or “Are there…?”.
8.model:
Hi Tatiana,

I'm moving to Cartagena next month! I have some questions about your neighbourhood. Is there a gym near your house? Are there any good schools for my son? How many buses go to the centre? How much traffic is there in the morning? How much is the rent for a small flat?

Thanks a lot!
Diego

8.title: Directions to my house
8.brief: A friend is coming to your house for the first time. Write directions from the bus stop or the metro station.
8.briefEs: Un amigo irá a tu casa por primera vez. Escribe las indicaciones desde la parada de bus o la estación del metro.
criteria: Use imperatives (Turn left, Go straight on…).
Use prepositions of place (next to, opposite, behind).
Mention two places on the way.
8.model: Get off the bus at the Central Park stop. Go straight on for two blocks. Turn left at the bakery. My street is the second on the right. My house is number 14. It is opposite the school and next to a small shop. It has a green door. Call me if you can't find it!

8.title: My ideal town
8.brief: Describe your ideal town. Say what there is and what there isn’t.
8.briefEs: Describe tu pueblo ideal. Di qué hay y qué no hay.
criteria: Use “There is / There are” at least four times.
Use “There isn’t / aren’t” once.
Use three prepositions of place.
8.model: In my ideal town, there is a big park in the centre. There are many trees and a lake. There is a library next to the park and there are two cinemas near the station. There isn't a lot of traffic and there aren't any tall buildings. Opposite the school, there is a pool for everybody.

8.title: At the tourist office
8.brief: You are in a new city. Write a dialogue at the tourist office: ask where two places are and how to get there.
8.briefEs: Estás en una ciudad nueva. Escribe un diálogo en la oficina de turismo: pregunta dónde están dos lugares y cómo llegar.
criteria: Use “Where is…?” and “Is there a…?”.
Use two prepositions of place (next to, opposite, near).
Say thank you at the end.
8.model:
Tourist: Excuse me, where is the museum?
Officer: It's near the cathedral, opposite the big park.
Tourist: Is there a café near the museum?
Officer: Yes, there is. It's next to the museum.
Tourist: Is it far?
Officer: No, it's ten minutes on foot.
Tourist: Thank you very much!

8.title: Welcome to our school
8.brief: Write a short text for a school brochure for new students. Say what there is in the school and where things are.
8.briefEs: Escribe un texto corto para un folleto del colegio dirigido a estudiantes nuevos. Di qué hay en el colegio y dónde están las cosas.
criteria: Use “There is / There are” at least three times.
Use three prepositions of place (next to, opposite, behind…).
Name six places (library, canteen, gym…).
8.model: Welcome to our school! There is a big yard in the middle. The library is next to the main office and there are two computer rooms upstairs. The canteen is opposite the gym. There are twenty classrooms and there is a small garden behind the science lab. We hope you enjoy our school!

8.title: I'm lost!
8.brief: You are lost in your city and your friend is waiting for you. Write a message: say where you are and ask for help.
8.briefEs: Estás perdido en tu ciudad y tu amigo te espera. Escribe un mensaje: di dónde estás y pide ayuda.
criteria: Use “There is / There are / There aren’t”.
Use two prepositions of place.
Ask two questions with “Is there…?” or “Where is…?”.
8.model: Hi Carlos! I'm lost. I'm in a small street near a big church. There is a bakery on my left and a bank opposite. There aren't any signs. Is there a bus stop near your house? Where is the metro station? Please call me! I'm waiting next to the bakery.

8.title: A postcard from a small town
8.brief: You are visiting a small town. Write a postcard to your family and say what there is and what you like.
8.briefEs: Visitas un pueblo pequeño. Escribe una postal a tu familia y di qué hay y qué te gusta.
criteria: Use there is / there are at least twice.
Use two adjectives (quiet, beautiful, old).
Say one thing you like and one you don’t.
8.model: Dear family, I'm in Villa de Leyva. It's a small and beautiful town. There is a big square with a white church and there are many cafés. The streets are old and quiet. I love the food, but there isn't any internet in my hotel! See you on Sunday. Julián

9.title: Find me at the airport
9.brief: Someone you don't know is picking you up at the airport. Write a message describing what you look like and what you are wearing.
9.briefEs: Describe en un mensaje cómo eres físicamente y qué ropa llevas para que te reconozcan en el aeropuerto.
criteria: Describe hair and eyes (straight / curly, brown, long).
Use “I’m wearing…” with two clothes items.
Use a modifier with a present participle (the woman carrying a red bag).
9.model: Hi Mr. Clark, this is Natalia. I'm quite tall and slim. I have long, curly black hair and brown eyes. Today I'm wearing jeans, a white T-shirt and a yellow jacket. I'm the woman carrying a big green suitcase and standing next to the café. See you soon!

9.title: Who's who in the photo?
9.brief: Describe a family or group photo. Identify four people using phrases like “the man wearing…”, “the girl sitting…”.
9.briefEs: Describe una foto de grupo e identifica a cuatro personas con frases como “the man wearing…”.
criteria: Four modifiers with -ing participles (wearing, sitting, holding, standing).
Two appearance words: beard, moustache, middle-aged, good-looking.
Use “looks like” once to compare two people.
9.model: This is a photo of my family at Christmas. The middle-aged man wearing glasses is my uncle Hernán. The woman sitting next to him is my aunt. The boy holding the dog is my cousin Sebastián. He looks like his father: they both have a beard! The girl standing at the back with curly hair is me.

9.title: Me and my parents
9.brief: Write about who you take after in your family. Compare your appearance and personality with your mother or father.
9.briefEs: Escribe a quién te pareces en tu familia, en físico y en personalidad.
criteria: Use “take after” and “look like” correctly.
Use “be like” for personality (What is she like?).
Three appearance adjectives (tall, short, slim, well-built, curly…).
9.model: People say I take after my mother. I look like her: we are both short and slim, and we have straight dark hair. But my eyes are green like my father's. In personality, I'm like my dad. He is calm and funny, and I am too. My brother looks like my dad: he is tall and well-built.

9.title: Describe my brother or sister
9.brief: Describe a brother, sister or cousin: age, height, hair, eyes and clothes.
9.briefEs: Describe a un hermano, hermana o primo: edad, estatura, cabello, ojos y ropa.
criteria: Use “has” for hair and eyes.
Use “is tall / short / thin…”.
Describe clothes with “is wearing”.
9.model: My sister Laura is fifteen. She is tall and thin. She has long, curly black hair and big brown eyes. She is very pretty. Today she is wearing a yellow T-shirt, blue jeans and white trainers. She is friendly and funny. We look different, but we are very good friends.

9.title: Lost: a missing person at the mall
9.brief: A child is lost at a shopping centre. Write the announcement to find him. Describe his looks and clothes.
9.briefEs: Un niño se perdió en un centro comercial. Escribe el anuncio para encontrarlo. Describe su apariencia y su ropa.
criteria: Give name and age.
Describe hair, eyes and height.
Say what he is wearing.
9.model: Attention, please. We are looking for a boy called Mateo. He is six years old. He is small and he has short brown hair and green eyes. He is wearing a red jacket, grey shorts and black shoes. He has a blue backpack. Please bring him to the information desk.

9.title: A comic book character
9.brief: Invent a character for a comic book. Describe his or her looks, clothes and personality.
9.briefEs: Inventa un personaje para un cómic. Describe su aspecto, su ropa y su personalidad.
criteria: Use “has” for hair and eyes.
Describe clothes with “is wearing”.
Use two adjectives for personality.
9.model: My character is Captain Luz. She is tall and strong. She has long red hair and green eyes. She is wearing a blue suit, a yellow cape and black boots. She is brave and kind, but she is also very funny. She doesn't have a car. She has a small robot called Beto. He is her best friend.

9.title: A profile for a school website
9.brief: Write your own profile for the school website: how you look, your personality and your hobbies.
9.briefEs: Escribe tu propio perfil para la página del colegio: cómo eres físicamente, tu personalidad y tus pasatiempos.
criteria: Describe your looks with “I have…” and “I am…”.
Use three adjectives for personality.
Say two hobbies.
9.model: Hi! I'm Valentina and I'm thirteen. I'm of medium height and I have long brown hair and brown eyes. I'm friendly, shy and creative. I like drawing and I love reading adventure books. I don't like football, but I like swimming. My best friend says I look like my mum!

9.title: What does he look like?
9.brief: You can't go to the airport to meet your uncle, so your friend is going. Write a message to your friend and describe what your uncle looks like so he can find him.
9.briefEs: No puedes ir al aeropuerto a recibir a tu tío, así que va tu amigo. Escribe un mensaje a tu amigo y describe cómo es tu tío para que lo reconozca.
criteria: Use “He is…” and “He has…”.
Describe hair and clothes.
Say where he is waiting.
9.model: Hi Sam! My uncle is arriving at the airport at five. He is tall and he has grey hair and a big moustache. He is wearing a brown coat and a blue cap. He has a black suitcase. He is waiting near the coffee shop. Please say hello for me!

9.title: Two friends compared
9.brief: Describe two friends and how they are different. Use look, have, is and are.
9.briefEs: Describe a dos amigos y en qué se diferencian. Usa look, have, is y are.
criteria: Use “but” to show differences.
Describe hair, height and personality.
Use “They both…” once.
9.model: My friends Ana and Lucía are very different. Ana is short and she has straight blonde hair. Lucía is tall and she has curly black hair. Ana is quiet, but Lucía is very talkative. They both have brown eyes and they both love music. I like them because they are kind.

10.title: Ready for the trip?
10.brief: You are travelling tomorrow. Write a message to your travel partner saying what you have already done and what you haven't done yet.
10.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje diciendo qué has hecho ya y qué no has hecho todavía antes de un viaje.
criteria: Three sentences with “already” before the past participle.
Two negative sentences with “yet” at the end.
Use “to book” and “to pack”.
10.model: Hi Andrea! Good news: I've already booked the hotel and I've already printed the tickets. I've just bought sunscreen too. But I haven't packed my suitcase yet and I haven't changed money yet. Have you finished your packing? Have you called the taxi yet? See you at 5 a.m.!

10.title: Things I have never done
10.brief: Write about your experiences: things you have done and things you have never done. Give one detail in the past simple for one experience.
10.briefEs: Escribe sobre experiencias que has tenido y que nunca has tenido, con un detalle en pasado simple.
criteria: Use “have ever / have never” + past participle three times.
One sentence in the past simple with a specific time (in 2022, last year).
Correct participles: been, seen, eaten, flown.
10.model: I have travelled a lot in Colombia, but I have never been outside the country. I have never flown in a small plane. Have I ever eaten something strange? Yes! I have eaten hormigas culonas. I ate them in Santander in 2022 and they were delicious. I have never seen snow, but I hope to see it one day.

10.title: A progress email to my boss
10.brief: Write a short email to your boss about a project. Say what you have finished so far and what you have not completed yet.
10.briefEs: Escribe un correo a tu jefe diciendo qué has terminado y qué no has completado aún en un proyecto.
criteria: Use “so far” and “just” once each.
Two sentences with “already” and two with “yet”.
A correct email greeting and closing.
10.model:
Dear Mrs. Gómez,

So far, I have finished the sales report and I have already sent it to the team. I have just called the new clients. I haven't completed the presentation yet, and I haven't booked the meeting room yet. I can finish them tomorrow.

Best regards,
Carlos

10.title: My to-do list
10.brief: Write about your to-do list for today. Say what you have done and what you haven’t done yet.
10.briefEs: Escribe sobre tu lista de tareas de hoy. Di qué has hecho y qué no has hecho todavía.
criteria: Use “I’ve + past participle” three times.
Use “I haven’t … yet” twice.
Use “already” once.
10.model: Today is a busy day. I've already made my bed and I've had breakfast. I've washed the dishes, too. But I haven't done my homework yet. I haven't cleaned my room yet and I haven't called my grandma. I want to do everything this afternoon.

10.title: Have you ever...?
10.brief: Write six “Have you ever…?” questions for a classmate about places, food and animals.
10.briefEs: Escribe seis preguntas “Have you ever…?” para un compañero sobre lugares, comida y animales.
criteria: Use “Have you ever + past participle?” six times.
Ask about three different topics.
Use correct participles (been, eaten, seen).
10.model: Have you ever been to the beach? Have you ever eaten sushi? Have you ever seen a whale? Have you ever flown in a plane? Have you ever met a famous person? Have you ever ridden a horse?

10.title: A postcard: what we've already seen
10.brief: You are on holiday in a city. Write a postcard to a friend. Say what you have already done and what you haven’t done yet.
10.briefEs: Estás de vacaciones en una ciudad. Escribe una postal a un amigo. Di qué has hecho ya y qué no has hecho todavía.
criteria: Use “already” and “yet”.
Use three present perfect verbs.
Start with Hi / Dear and finish with “Big hugs” and your name.
10.model:
Hi Elena!

We're in Cartagena and we're having a great time. We've already visited the old city and we've eaten fresh fish. I've taken a hundred photos! But we haven't been to the islands yet. My brother hasn't tried the coconut ice cream yet. We're going there tomorrow.

Big hugs,
Julián

10.title: A restaurant review: what I've tried
10.brief: You have eaten at a restaurant three times. Write a short review: what you have tried and what you haven’t tried yet.
10.briefEs: Has comido tres veces en un restaurante. Escribe una reseña corta: qué has probado y qué no has probado todavía.
criteria: Use “I’ve tried” and “I haven’t tried … yet”.
Use three present perfect verbs.
Finish with stars.
10.model: I've been to Sabor Criollo three times, and I love it. I've tried the chicken soup and the fried fish. Both are delicious. I haven't tried the desserts yet, but my sister has eaten the chocolate cake and she loves it. The waiters have always been friendly. I haven't found any problems yet. I give it five stars!

10.title: An end-of-term message
10.brief: The term is finishing. Write a message to a classmate: what you have learned and what you haven’t done yet.
10.briefEs: El periodo termina. Escribe un mensaje a un compañero: qué has aprendido y qué no has hecho todavía.
criteria: Use “We’ve / I’ve + past participle” three times.
Use “haven’t … yet” twice.
Ask “Have you…?” once.
10.model: Hi Sara! The term is almost over. We've learned a lot of English! I've finished all my homework and I've read two stories. I haven't practised my speaking yet, so can we study together? We haven't visited the school garden yet, either. Have you finished your project? I haven't started mine!

10.title: Have you finished yet?
10.brief: Write a chat between two friends who are preparing a school project. They ask what is finished and what is not.
10.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos amigos que preparan un proyecto escolar. Se preguntan qué está terminado y qué no.
criteria: Use “Have you … yet?” twice.
Answer with “Yes, I have” and “No, I haven’t”.
Write at least six lines.
10.model:
A: Have you finished the poster yet?
B: Yes, I have. I've drawn the map.
A: Have you written the text yet?
B: No, I haven't. Have you?
A: Yes, I've written two paragraphs.
B: Perfect! I've already printed the photos.
A: Have you printed the title yet?
B: No, I haven't. I can do it tonight.

11.title: Recommend a place in my city
11.brief: A tourist asks you for a recommendation in your city. Write a short message recommending a place to visit and a place to eat.
11.briefEs: Recomienda a un turista un lugar para visitar y uno para comer en tu ciudad.
criteria: Use “You should…” and “You can…” at least once each.
Use two adverbs before adjectives (really, quite, extremely).
Connect ideas with “because” and “so”.
11.model: You should visit Monserrate because the view is really amazing. You can take the cable car, so it's quite easy. Go early, because it's extremely crowded on Sundays. After that, you can eat at La Puerta Falsa. The tamales are really good and it's pretty cheap. It's worth it!

11.title: A short hotel review
11.brief: Write a review of a hotel or hostel you stayed in. Say what was good and what was bad, and recommend it or not.
11.briefEs: Escribe una reseña corta de un hotel donde te quedaste: lo bueno, lo malo y si lo recomiendas.
criteria: Use “however” or “though” to contrast.
Three adverb + adjective pairs (a bit noisy, really clean…).
Finish with a recommendation using “should” or “recommend”.
11.model:
Hotel Mar Azul, Santa Marta ★★★★
The rooms were really clean and the staff were extremely friendly. The breakfast was quite good. However, the street was a bit noisy at night. The pool was small, though it was nice. I recommend this hotel because the price is pretty low. You should ask for a room at the back.

11.title: Advice for a new student
11.brief: A new student is joining your English class. Write a message with three pieces of advice.
11.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje con tres consejos para un estudiante nuevo de tu clase de inglés.
criteria: Three sentences with “should” or “shouldn’t”.
One sentence with “can” for possibility.
Use “because” to explain one piece of advice.
11.model: Welcome to the class, Simón! Here is some advice. You should arrive early because the teacher starts on time. You shouldn't use your phone in class. You should do the homework: it's really useful. If you have questions, you can write in our group chat. Everyone is quite friendly here!

11.title: Advice for a tired friend
11.brief: Your friend is always tired at school. Write a message with four pieces of advice.
11.briefEs: Tu amigo siempre está cansado en el colegio. Escribe un mensaje con cuatro consejos.
criteria: Use “You should / shouldn’t”.
Give four different pieces of advice.
Use “because” once.
11.model: Hi Leo! You look tired. You should go to bed earlier, at about ten o'clock. You shouldn't use your phone in bed because the light isn't good for your sleep. You should drink more water and eat a good breakfast. And you shouldn't drink soda at night. I hope you feel better!

11.title: A film I recommend
11.brief: Recommend a film or a book to a friend. Say what it is about and give two reasons why he or she should see or read it.
11.briefEs: Recomienda una película o un libro a un amigo. Di de qué trata y da dos razones por las que debería verla o leerlo.
criteria: Use “You should…” and “You shouldn’t…”.
Give two reasons with “because”.
Say what the film or book is about.
11.model: You should watch 'The Little Dragon'. It's an animated film about a small dragon and a brave girl. You should see it because the story is funny and the music is beautiful. You shouldn't watch it at night if you are tired, because it is long. It is two hours! Take some popcorn and enjoy it with your family.

11.title: Tips for learning English
11.brief: Write five tips for a new English student. Use should and shouldn’t.
11.briefEs: Escribe cinco consejos para un estudiante nuevo de inglés. Usa should y shouldn’t.
criteria: Use “should” three times and “shouldn’t” twice.
Give practical advice (watch, read, speak…).
Use one linking word (and, but, because).
11.model: If you want to learn English, you should listen to songs and watch films with subtitles. You should read a little every day. You should speak with your friends, even if you make mistakes. You shouldn't be afraid of mistakes. You shouldn't study for many hours in one day, because short lessons are better.

11.title: A letter to a worried student
11.brief: A younger student is nervous about a test. Write a short letter to calm him or her down and give advice.
11.briefEs: Un estudiante menor está nervioso por un examen. Escríbele una carta corta para tranquilizarlo y darle consejos.
criteria: Use “You should…” twice.
Use “Don’t worry” once.
End with a kind sentence.
11.model: Dear Pablo, Don't worry about your test! You should study a little every day and you should sleep well the night before. You shouldn't study until midnight. On the day, you should have a good breakfast and take two pens. Remember: you are clever and you can do it. Good luck! Your friend, Ana

11.title: A reply to an advice column
11.brief: A teenager writes to a school magazine: “I have a problem. I can’t make friends in my new school.” Write a reply with three pieces of advice.
11.briefEs: Un adolescente escribe a la revista del colegio: “Tengo un problema. No logro hacer amigos en mi colegio nuevo.” Escribe una respuesta con tres consejos.
criteria: Use “You should” twice and “You shouldn’t” once.
Start with Dear and finish with a closing.
Include one kind or encouraging sentence.
11.model:
Dear Alex,

Don't worry! Many students feel the same way in a new school. You should smile and say hello to your classmates. You should join a club, like music or football. You shouldn't spend all your time alone with your phone. Talk to one person every day. Soon you are going to have new friends. Good luck!

Your friend,
The magazine team

11.title: A healthy week
11.brief: Write a short text for a school magazine with advice for a healthy week: food, sleep and sport.
11.briefEs: Escribe un texto corto para la revista del colegio con consejos para una semana saludable: comida, sueño y deporte.
criteria: Use “You should” and “You shouldn’t”.
Mention food, sleep and sport.
Write at least five sentences.
11.model: Do you want a healthy week? You should eat fruit and vegetables every day. You shouldn't eat too many sweets. You should sleep eight hours and you should play sport three times a week. You shouldn't spend all day on your phone. A healthy life is a happy life!

12.title: Plans for Saturday
12.brief: Write a message to your group of friends suggesting different plans for Saturday. Give two options and ask what they prefer.
12.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje al grupo de amigos proponiendo dos planes para el sábado y pregunta cuál prefieren.
criteria: Use “Let’s…” and “Why don’t we…?”.
Use “How about + -ing?” once.
Ask a question with “prefer”.
12.model: Hi guys! What should we do on Saturday? Let's go to the new pizza place. Or why don't we go to the cinema instead? How about meeting at the park first and having a picnic? Who's up for it? Which plan do you prefer? Maybe we can vote!

12.title: Can I borrow it?
12.brief: Write an email to a friend asking for a favour: you want to borrow something. Explain why, and say when you can give it back.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo pidiéndole prestado algo; explica por qué y cuándo lo devuelves.
criteria: Use “Could you lend me…?” or “Can I borrow…?”.
Use the word “favour”.
Use the difference borrow / lend correctly.
12.model:
Hi Martín,

Can I ask you a favour? My computer is broken and I have an exam on Friday. Could you lend me your laptop for two days? I can borrow my sister's, but she needs it for work. I can give it back on Saturday morning. Thank you so much!

Laura

12.title: Ideas for a class party
12.brief: Your class is planning an end-of-course party. Write suggestions about the place, food and music.
12.briefEs: Escribe sugerencias para la fiesta de fin de curso: lugar, comida y música.
criteria: Three suggestions with “could” or “should”.
One recommendation with an infinitive (It's a good idea to…).
Use “instead” or “maybe” once.
12.model: Here are my ideas for our party. We could have it in the school garden instead of the classroom. It's a good idea to bring food from different regions: I can bring empanadas. We should ask Diana to choose the music because she is a DJ. Maybe we could also play karaoke in English!

12.title: A note for the suggestion box
12.brief: Write a note for the school suggestion box. Make three suggestions to improve break time.
12.briefEs: Escribe una nota para el buzón de sugerencias del colegio. Haz tres sugerencias para mejorar el recreo.
criteria: Use “Let’s…” and “Shall we…?”.
Use “We can…” once.
Finish with thanks.
12.model:
Dear Principal,

I have some ideas for break time. Let's have music in the yard on Fridays. Shall we buy more balls for football and basketball? We can also paint a big chess board on the floor. Could we have more benches, too? I think these changes can make break time better. Thank you for reading my note.

Valeria, Class 6A

12.title: Can I sleep at your house?
12.brief: You want to stay at a friend's house on Saturday night. Write a message to your parents to ask for permission and make a plan.
12.briefEs: Quieres quedarte en casa de una amiga el sábado en la noche. Escribe un mensaje a tus padres para pedir permiso y hacer un plan.
criteria: Use “Can I…?” and “Could you…?”.
Give two reasons or plans.
Use “Let’s…” once.
12.model: Hi Mum and Dad! Can I stay at Lucía's house on Saturday night? Her mother says it is OK. We want to make pizza and watch a film. Let's call Lucía's mum tomorrow to talk. I can finish my homework on Friday, so I'm free on Saturday. Could you take me there at five? I can come home on Sunday morning. Please say yes!

12.title: Ideas for a class trip
12.brief: Your teacher asks for ideas for a class trip. Write four suggestions with reasons.
12.briefEs: Tu profesora pide ideas para una excursión. Escribe cuatro sugerencias con razones.
criteria: Use “Let’s…” or “We can…” four times.
Add a reason with “because”.
Choose different places.
12.model: Dear Ms Rojas, here are my ideas for the class trip. Let's go to the science museum because it has many experiments. We can visit the zoo and see the animals. Let's go to the beach, because it is fun. We can also go to the mountains for a picnic. I think all the ideas are good!

12.title: A charity walk poster
12.brief: Make a poster to invite people to a charity walk in your neighbourhood. Say when, where and why, and use suggestions.
12.briefEs: Crea un cartel para invitar a una caminata solidaria en tu barrio. Di cuándo, dónde y para qué, y usa sugerencias.
criteria: Use “Let’s…” and “Shall we…?”.
Say the date, the time and the place.
Use “We can…” once.
12.model: LET'S WALK FOR OUR PARK! Join us on Sunday, 4 May, at 8:00 in the morning. We meet at the main gate. Shall we walk for one hour? We can bring water and wear comfortable shoes. Let's plant ten new trees at the end! Children, parents and dogs are welcome. Tell your friends and come with your family. See you there!

12.title: Excuses and alternatives
12.brief: A friend invites you to the cinema, but you can’t go. Write a message to say no politely and suggest another day.
12.briefEs: Un amigo te invita al cine, pero no puedes ir. Escribe un mensaje para decir que no con cortesía y proponer otro día.
criteria: Use “Sorry, I can’t” and give a reason.
Use “Let’s…” for another plan.
Thank your friend.
12.model: Hi Sara! Thanks for the invitation. Sorry, I can't go to the cinema on Friday, because I have a family dinner. Can we go on Saturday? Let's see the film at four. I can ask my mum for money. Please tell me if that is OK. See you!

12.title: A welcome day for new students
12.brief: New students are coming to your school. Write four suggestions to make them feel welcome.
12.briefEs: Llegarán estudiantes nuevos a tu colegio. Escribe cuatro sugerencias para que se sientan bienvenidos.
criteria: Use “Let’s…” twice.
Use “We can…” twice.
Use “Shall we…?” once.
12.model: Let's make a welcome day for the new students! We can give them a small map of the school. Shall we ask them to sit with us at lunch? Let's make name tags for everybody. We can also introduce our teachers and show the library. I can write a welcome card. What do you think? The new students are going to be happy.

13.title: Me too! A reply to a profile
13.brief: Read this profile: “I love rock music. I don't like cold weather. I can cook well.” Write a reply saying if you agree or not with each sentence.
13.briefEs: Responde a un perfil diciendo si coincides o no con cada frase usando so, too, neither, either.
criteria: Use “So do I / Me too” once.
Use “Neither do I / Me neither” for a negative sentence.
Use one disagreement (I don’t. / I do!).
13.model: Hi! I read your profile. You love rock music? So do I! My favourite band is Aterciopelados. You don't like cold weather? Neither do I. I prefer the beach. You can cook well? Well, I can't! I usually burn the rice. Maybe you can teach me!

13.title: A polite request to a neighbour
