13.brief: Write a polite note to your neighbour. Ask him or her to do two things (turn down the music, move the car…).
13.briefEs: Escribe una nota amable a un vecino pidiéndole dos cosas con “would”.
criteria: Use “Would you…, please?” and “Would you mind + -ing?”.
Use “Thank you” and a friendly closing.
Explain the reason with “because”.
13.model:
Dear neighbour,

Would you turn down the music after 10 p.m., please? I start work very early, so I need to sleep. Also, would you mind moving your car a little? It's in front of my garage door. Thank you very much, and no problem if you need anything from me!

Teresa, apartment 4B

13.title: My opinion about school uniforms
13.brief: Write a short opinion about school uniforms. Say what you think and if you agree or disagree with other people.
13.briefEs: Escribe una opinión corta sobre los uniformes escolares y di si estás de acuerdo con otras personas.
criteria: Use “I think” and “I don’t think”.
Use “agree / disagree” once each.
Use “actually” to add a surprising idea.
13.model: I think school uniforms are a good idea. Many parents say they are expensive, but I don't agree. Actually, uniforms are cheaper than new clothes every week. My friend thinks uniforms are boring. I agree with her a little, but I don't think clothes are important at school. In my opinion, students should study, not show fashion.

13.title: Me too, me neither
13.brief: Write a chat between two friends who discover they have a lot in common. Use “Me too” and “Me neither”.
13.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos amigos que descubren que tienen muchas cosas en común. Usa “Me too” y “Me neither”.
criteria: Use “Me too” twice.
Use “Me neither” twice.
Use “I like / I don’t like”.
13.model:
A: I like pizza.
B: Me too! I love it.
A: I don't like spicy food.
B: Me neither!
A: I don't like Mondays.
B: Me neither!
A: I can't swim.
B: Me neither, but I can ride a bike.
A: Me too! Let's ride bikes on Saturday.
B: Great idea!

13.title: Do you agree?
13.brief: Write your opinion about homework on weekends. Say if you agree or disagree and give two reasons.
13.briefEs: Escribe tu opinión sobre la tarea del fin de semana. Di si estás de acuerdo o no y da dos razones.
criteria: Use “I think…” and “In my opinion…”.
Give two reasons with “because”.
Use “I agree / I don’t agree”.
13.model: I think students shouldn't have homework on weekends. In my opinion, we need to rest, because we work hard all week. We also need time with our family. Some people say homework helps us learn. I don't agree, because we can learn by playing sport or reading a book. What do you think?

13.title: Giving up a seat
13.brief: On a crowded bus, an old woman is standing. Write a polite dialogue with a young person who offers a seat. Use polite requests and thanks.
13.briefEs: En un bus lleno, una señora mayor va de pie. Escribe un diálogo cortés con un joven que le ofrece su asiento. Usa peticiones corteses y agradecimientos.
criteria: Use “Could I…?” and “Could you…?”.
Use please and thank you.
Write at least six lines.
13.model:
Boy: Excuse me, would you like to sit down?
Woman: Oh, thank you! That's very kind.
Boy: Could I carry your bag, too?
Woman: Yes, please. It's a bit heavy.
Boy: No problem. Is this your stop?
Woman: Yes, it is. Could you open the door for me?
Boy: Of course. Take care!

13.title: My favourite things (and yours)
13.brief: Write about four things you like and four things you don’t like. Say what your best friend thinks, too.
13.briefEs: Escribe sobre cuatro cosas que te gustan y cuatro que no. Di también qué piensa tu mejor amigo.
criteria: Use “So do I / Neither do I” or “Me too / Me neither”.
Use “but” to compare.
Use love, like, don’t like, hate.
13.model: I love music and I like animals. I like pizza and I love football. I don't like spiders and I hate cold weather. I don't like Maths and I hate getting up early. My best friend loves music. So do I! She doesn't like spiders. Neither do I! But she likes Maths, and I don't. We agree on many things, so we are great friends.

13.title: A free Friday: yes or no?
13.brief: Write your opinion about a school week of four days, with no school on Fridays. Give two reasons for your idea.
13.briefEs: Escribe tu opinión sobre una semana escolar de cuatro días, sin clases los viernes. Da dos razones para tu idea.
criteria: Start with “In my opinion…”.
Give two reasons with “First” and “Second”.
End with a conclusion.
13.model: In my opinion, a school week of four days is a good idea. First, students can rest more, so we are happier on Monday. Second, we can spend more time with our family. Some people think we learn less, but I don't agree. We can study at home on Fridays. So I say yes to a free Friday.

13.title: Comments under a video
13.brief: Read three comments under a video about school food: “I love pizza day!”, “I don’t like fish.” and “I can’t eat spicy food.” Write your reply to each comment.
13.briefEs: Lee tres comentarios bajo un video sobre la comida del colegio: “¡Amo el día de pizza!”, “No me gusta el pescado.” y “No puedo comer picante.” Escribe tu respuesta a cada comentario.
criteria: Use “Me too” once and “Me neither” twice.
Add a reason after each reply.
Ask one question at the end.
13.model:
1. Me too! I love pizza day and it's my favourite lunch.
2. Me neither! I don't like fish. It smells strange.
3. Me neither! I can't eat spicy food. It makes me cough. But I like soup. What about you?

14.title: The highest and the biggest
14.brief: Write five fun facts about the geography of Colombia or another country. Use superlatives and measurements.
14.briefEs: Escribe cinco datos curiosos sobre la geografía de Colombia u otro país con superlativos y medidas.
criteria: Four superlatives with “the” (the highest, the longest, the most beautiful).
Two measurements with metres or kilometres.
Use one of: by far, roughly, twice as… as.
14.model: Colombia is an amazing country. The highest mountain is Pico Cristóbal Colón: it's roughly 5,700 metres high. The longest river is the Magdalena, about 1,500 kilometres long. Caño Cristales is by far the most colourful river in the world. La Guajira has the driest desert in the country. The Amazon is the biggest rainforest on Earth.

14.title: Two cities compared
14.brief: Compare two cities you know (e.g. Bogotá and Cartagena): weather, size, population, coast. Say which is the best for a holiday.
14.briefEs: Compara dos ciudades (clima, tamaño, población, costa) y di cuál es la mejor para vacaciones.
criteria: Three comparatives and two superlatives.
Include the words dry / humid, coast, population.
Use “twice as… as” or “much” before a comparative.
14.model: Bogotá is much bigger than Cartagena. Its population is about eight million: that's eight times as big. Bogotá is colder and drier, and Cartagena is hotter and more humid. Cartagena is on the coast, so its beaches are the best part. For a holiday, I think Cartagena is the most fun city in Colombia.

14.title: Questions for a travel quiz
14.brief: Write a travel quiz with six questions about measurements and records. Give the answers at the end.
14.briefEs: Escribe un concurso de seis preguntas sobre medidas y récords geográficos con sus respuestas.
criteria: Use “How high / How long / How deep / How big…?”.
Two questions with a superlative (What is the longest…?).
Answers with numbers and units.
14.model:
Travel Quiz!
1. How high is Mount Everest?
2. How long is the Amazon River?
3. What is the largest desert in the world?
4. How deep is Lake Titicaca?
5. Which is the biggest ocean?
6. How far is Bogotá from Medellín?
Answers: 1. 8,849 metres. 2. About 6,400 km. 3. Antarctica. 4. 281 metres. 5. The Pacific. 6. Roughly 415 km.

14.title: The best in my class
14.brief: Write about the best students in your class in different things: the tallest, the funniest, the fastest and the best at English.
14.briefEs: Escribe sobre los mejores de tu clase en diferentes cosas: el más alto, el más gracioso, el más rápido y el mejor en inglés.
criteria: Use four superlatives (the tallest, the funniest…).
Use “the best” once.
Use names of classmates.
14.model: In my class, Diego is the tallest student. Camila is the funniest girl, because she always makes jokes. Juan is the fastest runner in the school. Sofía is the best at English and she is also the quietest. I'm not the best at anything, but I'm the happiest person in the class!

14.title: Amazing animals
14.brief: Write about three animals: the biggest, the fastest and the most dangerous. Use superlatives.
14.briefEs: Escribe sobre tres animales: el más grande, el más rápido y el más peligroso. Usa superlativos.
criteria: Use “the biggest / the fastest / the most dangerous”.
Add one fact for each animal.
Use “is / are” correctly.
14.model: The blue whale is the biggest animal in the world. It is as long as two or three buses! The cheetah is the fastest land animal. It can run at 100 kilometres an hour. The most dangerous animal for people is the mosquito, because it carries diseases. Animals are amazing and we should protect them.

14.title: The best place in my country
14.brief: Describe the most beautiful place in your country. Say why it is the best.
14.briefEs: Describe el lugar más bonito de tu país. Di por qué es el mejor.
criteria: Use “the most beautiful” or “the biggest”.
Give two reasons.
Use at least three adjectives.
14.model: For me, the most beautiful place in Colombia is the Cocora Valley. It has the tallest palm trees in the world. The weather is cool and the views are amazing. It is also one of the cleanest places I know. You can ride horses and walk for hours. It is the best place for a family trip.

14.title: A school awards certificate
14.brief: Write a certificate for the ‘best’ students in your class. Give four awards, each one with a superlative and a reason.
14.briefEs: Escribe un certificado para los ‘mejores’ estudiantes de tu clase. Da cuatro premios, cada uno con un superlativo y una razón.
criteria: Use at least four superlatives.
Give a reason for each award.
Use the names of classmates.
14.model: SCHOOL AWARDS – CLASS 6C. The Funniest Student: Marco, because he makes the best jokes. The Fastest Runner: Isabela, who is the quickest girl in the school. The Kindest Friend: Gabi, because he always helps everybody. The Most Creative Artist: Sol, who paints the most beautiful pictures. Congratulations to all!

14.title: My best, worst and favourite
14.brief: Write about the best and the worst things in your week: food, film, day and lesson.
14.briefEs: Escribe sobre lo mejor y lo peor de tu semana: comida, película, día y clase.
criteria: Use “the best” and “the worst”.
Cover four topics.
Add a reason for two of them.
14.model: The best day of my week is Friday, because we finish early. The worst day is Monday. The best food at school is pizza and the worst is cold soup. The best lesson is Art, because I can draw. The worst lesson is Maths. I think the best film this week is the animal adventure.

14.title: A theme park review
14.brief: Write a review of a theme park. Say which are the best, the scariest and the slowest rides, and give it stars.
14.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un parque de diversiones. Di cuáles son las mejores, las más aterradoras y las más lentas atracciones, y dale estrellas.
criteria: Use at least five superlatives.
Use “but” once to show a bad point.
Finish with stars.
14.model: Fantasy Land is the best park in our region. The roller coaster is the fastest and the scariest ride. I love it! The water slide is the funniest, but the queue is the longest. The carousel is the slowest and the most relaxing ride. It's perfect for small children. The food is expensive, but the park is the cleanest I know. I give it five stars.

15.title: Next week's plans
15.brief: Write a message to a friend who wants to meet. Explain your arrangements for next week and say when you are free.
15.briefEs: Escribe a un amigo tus planes de la próxima semana y dile cuándo estás libre.
criteria: Two arrangements with the present continuous (I’m meeting…).
Two plans with “be going to”.
Use “busy”, “available” or “appointment”.
15.model: Hi Pilar! Next week is very busy. On Monday I'm meeting my boss at 9:00. On Tuesday I have a dentist appointment. On Wednesday I'm going to visit my grandmother. On Thursday I'm flying to Cali. But I'm available on Friday! Are you going to be free? We're going to have fun!

15.title: Taking a phone message
15.brief: You answered the phone for your roommate. Write a note with the message from the caller. Use “said” and “told”.
15.briefEs: Escribe una nota para tu compañero de apartamento con el mensaje de alguien que llamó.
criteria: Use “said (that)” and “told me / asked me”.
Include a request: “asked you to call back”.
Include a time and a phone number.
15.model: Kevin, Mr. Torres from the bank called at 3:00. He said that your new card is ready. He told me the office closes at 5:00 today. He asked you to call him back before 4:30. His number is 601 555 2233. He also said you need to bring your ID. – Sofi

15.title: Sorry, I'm running late
15.brief: Write an email to your teacher. You are going to be late for class. Explain why, and ask him or her to remind you about the homework.
15.briefEs: Escribe un correo a tu profesor: vas a llegar tarde; explica por qué y pide que te recuerde la tarea.
criteria: Use “be running late” or “be about to”.
One sentence with “be going to”.
A polite request with “Could you…?”.
15.model:
Dear Professor Ruiz,

I'm sorry, but I'm running late. My bus broke down and I'm about to take a taxi. I'm going to arrive at 8:30. Could you remind me about the homework at the end of the class? Could you also tell my partner to start without me?

Thank you,
Esteban

15.title: My voicemail greeting
15.brief: Write the greeting for your phone voicemail. Say that you can’t answer, when you are going to call back, and ask the caller to leave a message.
15.briefEs: Escribe el saludo del buzón de voz de tu teléfono. Di que no puedes contestar, cuándo vas a devolver la llamada y pide a quien llama que deje un mensaje.
criteria: Use “I can’t…” and “I’m going to…”.
Say when you are going to call back.
Ask the caller to leave a message.
15.model: Hello! This is Ignacio. I can't answer the phone now because I'm in a football match. I'm going to call you back after six o'clock. Please leave your name, your number and a short message. If you need help, call my mum on 555 0147. Thanks for calling!

15.title: The weekend weather forecast
15.brief: You are a weather reporter. Write the forecast for the weekend using “going to” for predictions.
15.briefEs: Eres un reportero del clima. Escribe el pronóstico del fin de semana usando “going to” para las predicciones.
criteria: Use “It’s going to…” at least three times.
Use one negative (isn’t going to).
Mention three different days.
15.model: Here is the weather for this weekend. On Saturday, it's going to be hot and sunny, so you can go to the beach. In the afternoon, there are going to be some clouds. On Sunday, it's going to rain in the mountains. It isn't going to be cold, but you should take an umbrella. On Monday, it's going to be windy. Have a nice weekend!

15.title: A note on the fridge
15.brief: You are not going to be home for dinner. Write a note for your family on the fridge: where you are going, what you are going to do and when you are going to be back.
15.briefEs: No vas a estar en casa para la cena. Escribe una nota para tu familia en la nevera: adónde vas, qué vas a hacer y a qué hora vas a volver.
criteria: Use “I’m going to…” and “We’re going to…”.
Say when you are going to be back.
Use one negative with “not going to”.
15.model:
Mum and Dad,

I'm not going to be home for dinner tonight. I'm going to eat at Ana's house because we are going to study for the Science test. Her mum is going to make pasta. I'm going to come back at about nine. Ana's dad is going to bring me home by car. Please don't wait for me. I have my key.

Love,
Paula

15.title: An invitation to my party
15.brief: Write an invitation for your party. Include what, when, where and what you are going to do.
15.briefEs: Escribe una invitación para tu fiesta. Incluye qué, cuándo, dónde y qué van a hacer.
criteria: Say the date, time and place.
Use “We’re going to…” twice.
Ask for an answer (Please reply by…).
15.model: You are invited to my birthday party! It's on Saturday, 15 June, at four o'clock, at my house, 20 Pine Street. We're going to play games, eat pizza and dance. We're going to have a big chocolate cake, too. Please reply by Wednesday. I hope you can come! Sofía

15.title: A message to my teacher about tomorrow
15.brief: Write a short message to your teacher. Say that you are going to be late for school tomorrow and why.
15.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje corto a tu profesor. Di que mañana vas a llegar tarde al colegio y por qué.
criteria: Use “I’m going to be late”.
Give a reason.
Say what time you are going to arrive.
15.model: Dear Ms Díaz, I'm writing to tell you that I'm going to be late tomorrow. I have a dentist appointment at eight o'clock. I'm going to arrive at school at about ten. I'm going to ask my friend for the notes. I'm sorry about this. Thank you. Mario Suárez

15.title: A shopping plan for a party
15.brief: Your family is going to have a party next week. Write a message to your brother: what you are going to buy, where and when, and what he is going to do.
15.briefEs: Tu familia va a hacer una fiesta la próxima semana. Escribe un mensaje a tu hermano: qué vas a comprar, dónde y cuándo, y qué va a hacer él.
criteria: Use “going to” at least four times.
Use one negative (aren’t / isn’t going to).
Say where and when.
15.model: Hi Rubén! For Dad's party, I'm going to go to the supermarket on Thursday afternoon. I'm going to buy juice, bread and fruit. Can you buy the cake? You are going to pass the bakery on your way home. We aren't going to buy balloons because Mum has some. Dad is going to be very happy! Tell me if you need anything.

16.title: Then and now
16.brief: Compare your life ten years ago with your life now. Write about your home, your hobbies and your friends.
16.briefEs: Compara tu vida de hace diez años con tu vida actual: casa, pasatiempos y amigos.
criteria: Past simple for ten years ago (I lived, I had).
Present simple with “nowadays” or “these days”.
One sentence in the present perfect (I have changed…).
16.model: Ten years ago, I lived in a small town with my parents. I played football every day and I had two best friends. Back then, I didn't have a phone. Nowadays, I live in Bogotá with my wife. These days, I go to the gym and I read a lot. I have changed a lot, but I still love football.

16.title: My goals for next year
16.brief: Write about three goals you have for next year. Use verbs followed by infinitives.
16.briefEs: Escribe tres metas para el próximo año usando verbos seguidos de infinitivo.
criteria: Use four verb + infinitive patterns (hope to, want to, decide to, plan to).
Use “goal” and “to improve”.
Use “I’m looking forward to + -ing” once.
16.model: I have three goals for next year. First, I want to improve my English because I hope to get a better job. Second, I plan to save money for a trip to Mexico. Third, I've decided to learn to swim. I'm looking forward to travelling and meeting new people. I hope to finish all my goals!

16.title: A letter to my future self
16.brief: Write a short letter to yourself in five years. Describe your life now and say what you hope or plan to do.
16.briefEs: Escribe una carta corta a tu yo del futuro: describe tu vida ahora y lo que esperas hacer.
criteria: Present simple for your life now.
Two verb + infinitive patterns for plans (hope to, would like to).
One question to your future self in the present perfect (Have you…?).
16.model:
Dear future me,

Now I am 22 and I work in a shoe shop. I study English at night and I live with my parents. I hope to finish university soon and I would like to live in my own apartment. Have you visited London? Have you learned to drive? I hope you are happy!

Love,
Me

16.title: When I was five
16.brief: Compare your life when you were five with your life now: school, hobbies and food.
16.briefEs: Compara tu vida a los cinco años con tu vida ahora: colegio, pasatiempos y comida.
criteria: Use “used to” once or the past of “be”.
Use present simple for now.
Use “but now…” twice.
16.model: When I was five, I was very small and I used to love cartoons. I didn't go to school, but now I'm in Grade 8. I used to eat only pasta, but now I like many foods. I used to play with toys, and now I prefer video games. I used to cry a lot, but now I'm calm.

16.title: My dream job
16.brief: Write about the job you want to do in the future and what you need to do to get it.
16.briefEs: Escribe sobre el trabajo que quieres hacer en el futuro y qué necesitas hacer para conseguirlo.
criteria: Use “I want to…” and “I hope to…”.
Use “I need to…” once.
Say why you like this job.
16.model: I want to be a vet. I love animals and I want to help them. To get this job, I need to study hard at school and I need to go to university. I hope to work in a big animal hospital. I also plan to have a farm with horses. I'd like to start soon!

16.title: A goodbye message
16.brief: Your best friend is moving to another country. Write a goodbye message. Say what you hope to do together in the future.
16.briefEs: Tu mejor amiga se muda a otro país. Escribe un mensaje de despedida. Di qué esperas hacer con ella en el futuro.
criteria: Use hope to, want to and plan to.
Use “I’m looking forward to + -ing” once.
Start with Dear and finish with Love.
16.model:
Dear Camila,

I don't want to say goodbye. I'm very sad, but I'm happy for your new adventure. I hope to visit you next summer. I want to see your new school and your new house. I plan to write to you every week. Please remember to send me photos. I'm looking forward to seeing you again! You are my best friend.

Love,
Ana

16.title: A thank-you message to a teacher
16.brief: The school year is ending. Write a thank-you card to your favourite teacher. Say what you learned and what you hope to do next year.
16.briefEs: El año escolar termina. Escribe una tarjeta de agradecimiento a tu profesor favorito. Di qué aprendiste y qué esperas hacer el próximo año.
criteria: Use “thank you for + -ing”.
Use “I learned to…” and “I hope to…”.
Finish with a warm closing.
16.model: Dear Ms Torres, Thank you for teaching us this year. I learned to write short stories and I learned to speak with confidence. I hope to continue studying English next year. I want to visit your class again in the future. You are a wonderful teacher. With love, Camila

16.title: How my city has changed
16.brief: Write about how your city is different now from ten years ago. Use then and now.
16.briefEs: Escribe cómo es diferente tu ciudad ahora respecto de hace diez años. Usa then y now.
criteria: Use “There was / There were” for the past.
Use “Now there is / there are”.
Use “but now” once.
16.model: Ten years ago, there was only one small park in my city. There were few shops and there wasn't a metro. Now there are three parks, a big shopping centre and a new metro line. The streets are busier, but they are also cleaner. I like my city now.

16.title: A speech at the end of the year
16.brief: Write a short speech for the end of the school year. Thank your teachers and say what you learned and what you hope to do next year.
16.briefEs: Escribe un discurso corto para el final del año escolar. Agradece a tus profesores y di qué aprendiste y qué esperas hacer el próximo año.
criteria: Use “Thank you for + -ing”.
Use “I learned to…” once and “I hope / want / plan to…” twice.
Start with Good morning.
16.model: Good morning, everyone. This year was wonderful. Thank you, teachers, for helping us. I learned to write short stories and I learned to speak in front of the class. I also made new friends. Next year, I hope to improve my English and I want to join the school choir. I plan to read one book every month. Thank you all, and have a great holiday!
